issues.title: Helper function missing static keyword
issues.description: The rule requires that helper functions used only within a single source file should be declared with the 'static' keyword to limit their visibility to that compilation unit. The function addHashFieldToReply is only used within t_hash.c but is declared without 'static', making it unnecessarily visible to other compilation units.
issues.rule_name: Internal Helper Functions Must Be Declared Static

issues.title: HINCRBYFLOAT removes field expiration time locally on master
issues.description: The hincrbyfloatCommand function is missing the HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL flag when calling hashTypeSet. While the replication command correctly uses KEEPTTL to preserve field TTL for replicas and AOF, the local execution on the master immediately removes any existing field expiration time. This creates an inconsistency where the field loses its TTL on the master but the replicated HSETEX command attempts to keep it. The test at line 1987 expects field f1 to retain its TTL after HINCRBYFLOAT, but this bug causes the TTL to be cleared locally.

issues.title: Incorrect argument count in rewriteClientCommandVector causes malformed replication
issues.description: The rewriteClientCommandVector call passes 6 as the argument count, but actually provides 7 arguments (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, value). This mismatch causes the replication command to be truncated, omitting the final argument (the new field value). Replicas and AOF will receive an incomplete HSETEX command missing the field value, leading to command execution failures on replicas, replication inconsistencies, and potential data corruption. The test expects the replication stream to contain a complete HSETEX command with all arguments.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14224 - Fix HINCRBYFLOAT removes field expiration on replica

structured_output.summary: The PR changes HINCRBYFLOAT so the replicated form is `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value` instead of `HSET key field value`. The goal is to stop replicas from dropping a field's TTL when the master keeps it. The approach is sound, but the implementation has two defects that break the feature. First, `rewriteClientCommandVector` is called with `argc=6` while seven objects are passed, so the value argument is silently dropped and the replicated command is malformed. Second, the local `hashTypeSet` call loses `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`, so the master now strips the TTL of any field it increments. The added regression test cannot pass as written: its expected stream line has seven tokens, and it never checks the master's TTL after the increment.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two correctness bugs block merge. The argc mismatch produces a malformed HSETEX on the replication stream and AOF, which replicas cannot apply. Dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL changes master-side semantics, so HINCRBYFLOAT now destroys field expirations on the master, the opposite of the PR's intent. The test suite did not catch either problem because it only checks the replica view and never asserts the master's TTL after the increment.

architecture.overview:
HINCRBYFLOAT in `src/t_hash.c` computes the new value on the master, writes it to the in-memory hash, and then rewrites the client's argv so the command propagates to replicas and the AOF. Before this PR, the rewrite turned the command into `HSET key field value`, which clears any field TTL on replicas. The master keeps the TTL because the local write uses HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, which creates a divergence. The PR changes the rewrite to `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value` so replicas keep the TTL too. It also removes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL from the local write, which is the change that causes the master-side regression.

The rewrite path is shared with other commands: `rewriteClientCommandVector` copies a fixed number of argument objects into a new argv, and `propagateNow` serializes that argv to replicas and the AOF. Because the argument count is hard-coded, any mismatch between `argc` and the objects passed is invisible to the compiler and only shows up as a broken command stream.
steps: Entry point: `hincrbyfloatCommand` in `src/t_hash.c` reads the current field value, computes the sum, and writes the result with `hashTypeSet`. This is the local write path, and it decides whether the field TTL survives.

Local write: the PR removes `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` from the `hashTypeSet` call. In `hashTypeSet`, dropping that flag makes the code call `hfieldPersist` on the existing field (hashtable encoding) or override the expiry with `HASH_LP_NO_TTL` (listpack encoding). The master therefore loses the field's TTL.

Propagation rewrite: the PR replaces `rewriteClientCommandArgument` calls with one `rewriteClientCommandVector(c, 6, ...)` call that passes seven objects. Only six are read, so the value is dropped and the replicated command is `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field`.

Supporting changes: `server.c` and `server.h` add shared `hsetex` and `fields` objects so the rewrite does not allocate new strings. `addHashFieldToReply` loses `static` without a prototype. That change is unrelated to the fix.

Tests: the new test in `tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl` checks the replication stream and replica TTLs. It does not assert the master's TTL after `hincrbyfloat`, and its expected stream line cannot match the malformed command.

findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector called with argc=6 but seven objects, dropping the value
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` (around lines 2571-2572) calls `rewriteClientCommandVector(c, 6, ...)` but passes seven objects: `shared.hsetex`, `c->argv[1]`, `shared.keepttl`, `shared.fields`, `shared.integers[1]`, `c->argv[2]`, `newobj`. Change the argc to 7 so the new value is propagated. Check that the resulting command is `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value`. Follow the argc-matches-object-count pattern used in `src/t_string.c` near line 121.

findings.title: Removing HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL clears the master's field TTL on HINCRBYFLOAT
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` (around line 2559) calls `hashTypeSet` with only `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE`. The earlier version used `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`. Restore `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` so an increment on the master does not clear an existing field TTL. Keep the replication rewrite as it is. Then confirm `HTTL` on the master still returns the original TTL after `HINCRBYFLOAT`.

findings.title: Regression test checks only replica TTLs and cannot pass with the current rewrite
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl`, the new test near lines 1960-2005 checks the replication stream and replica TTLs only. Add an assertion on the master (`r`, not `r -1`) that `httl h1 FIELDS 1 f1` is still within 90..100 after `hincrbyfloat h1 f1 1.1`. Confirm the expected stream line `hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *` matches the real command after the argc fix in `src/t_hash.c`. Keep the existing structure and tags.

findings.title: Replicated and AOF command changes to HSETEX break older replicas and AOF readers
findings.body: HINCRBYFLOAT now propagates `HSETEX`, which exists only from Redis 8.0 (`commands.def` marks it `8.0.0`). Any replica or AOF reader on 7.4 or earlier cannot parse the new command. During a rolling upgrade where a 7.4 replica follows an 8.x master, or an AOF written by this build is loaded by 7.4, replication or loading will fail. The PR description notes the 7.4 branch is not fixed, but it does not call out this mixed-version risk. A release note or a version gate would make this explicit.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` now propagates HSETEX (around lines 2567-2573), which older replicas and AOF readers cannot parse. Document the mixed-version replication and AOF compatibility impact in the PR description or a release note. Decide whether a version gate (for example, a replica capability check) is needed before merge. Do not change the propagated command format in this fix unless the decision requires it.

findings.title: Unrelated visibility change: addHashFieldToReply lost static
findings.body:
`addHashFieldToReply` was changed from `static` to external linkage. It has no prototype in a header, and nothing in the PR needs it outside `t_hash.c`. The change exports an extra symbol and goes beyond the stated fix. Revert it unless there is a caller in another file, which I could not find.

::diff{file="src/t_hash.c" lines="2576-2576"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `addHashFieldToReply` (around line 2576) was changed from `static` to a non-static function with no prototype. Restore `static` unless a caller in another translation unit needs it. A grep for `addHashFieldToReply` finds only `t_hash.c` callers.

findings.title: Replication rewrite uses shared objects for the HSETEX tokens
findings.body: Adding `shared.hsetex`, `shared.fields` and reusing `shared.keepttl` and `shared.integers[1]` avoids per-call allocations for the constant tokens. The shared-object pattern matches existing code in `src/server.c` and `src/server.h`. The `shared.fields` name is generic, but it is only used in this rewrite.

findings.title: Keeping the normalized float value in the propagated command is the right design
findings.body: Propagating the final computed value instead of the increment preserves the PR's goal of avoiding float-precision and formatting divergence across replicas and AOF restarts. Using `KEEPTTL` in the propagated command also keeps the replica's field TTL intact. The design works once the two defects above are fixed.
